Portinari color and fill scales for ggplot2

Source: R/scales.R
portinari_scales.Rd

Discrete or continuous color and fill scales built from a Portinari palette. They are ordinary ggplot2 scales and accept the usual arguments (name, labels, breaks, guide, ...). Match the palette category to the data: qualitative palettes for unordered groups, sequential palettes for ordered values, and diverging palettes for values around a midpoint (see portinari.palettes()).

Usage

scale_color_portinari(
  palette = "cafe",
  type = c("discrete", "continuous"),
  direction = 1,
  colorblind = FALSE,
  ...
)

scale_colour_portinari(
  palette = "cafe",
  type = c("discrete", "continuous"),
  direction = 1,
  colorblind = FALSE,
  ...
)

scale_fill_portinari(
  palette = "cafe",
  type = c("discrete", "continuous"),
  direction = 1,
  colorblind = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

palette

Name of the palette. See portinari.palettes().

type

"discrete" (default) for categorical variables, or "continuous" for numeric variables.

direction

1 (default) or -1 to reverse the palette.

colorblind

If TRUE, only colorblind-safe colors are used.

...

Further arguments passed to ggplot2::discrete_scale() (discrete) or ggplot2::scale_colour_gradientn() / ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn() (continuous).

Value

A ggplot2 scale object.

See also

portinari.pal()

Examples

library(ggplot2)
#> Warning: package ‘ggplot2’ was built under R version 4.5.2
# Qualitative: unordered groups
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_portinari("cafe", name = "Cylinders")


# Sequential: ordered values
ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_portinari("guerra_azul", type = "continuous", direction = -1)


# Diverging: values around a midpoint
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, colour = mpg - mean(mpg))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_portinari("guerra", type = "continuous", name = "mpg vs mean")


# Diverging, discrete: an ordered scale with a neutral middle
ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(gear), fill = factor(carb))) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_portinari("retirantes")
